Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 05fe3c103f7e6b8b4fca8a7001dfc9ed4628085b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2022 14:47:52 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mm/usercopy: return 1 from hardened_usercopy __setup()
 handler

__setup() handlers should return 1 if the command line option is handled
and 0 if not (or maybe never return 0; it just pollutes init's
environment).  This prevents:

  Unknown kernel command line parameters \
  "BOOT_IMAGE=/boot/bzImage-517rc5 hardened_usercopy=off", will be \
  passed to user space.

  Run /sbin/init as init process
   with arguments:
     /sbin/init
   with environment:
     HOME=/
     TERM=linux
     BOOT_IMAGE=/boot/bzImage-517rc5
     hardened_usercopy=off
or
     hardened_usercopy=on
but when "hardened_usercopy=foo" is used, there is no Unknown kernel
command line parameter.

Return 1 to indicate that the boot option has been handled.
Print a warning if strtobool() returns an error on the option string,
but do not mark this as in unknown command line option and do not cause
init's environment to be polluted with this string.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20220222034249.14795-1-rdunlap@infradead.org
Link: lore.kernel.org/r/64644a2f-4a20-bab3-1e15-3b2cdd0defe3@omprussia.ru
Fixes: b5cb15d9372ab ("usercopy: Allow boot cmdline disabling of hardening")
Signed-off-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Reported-by: Igor Zhbanov <i.zhbanov@omprussia.ru>
Acked-by: Chris von Recklinghausen <crecklin@redhat.com>
Cc: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/usercopy.c b/mm/usercopy.c
index e7b0cb49daa1..bf4d57fefee1 100644
--- a/mm/usercopy.c
+++ b/mm/usercopy.c
@@ -284,7 +284,10 @@ static bool enable_checks __initdata = true;
 
 static int __init parse_hardened_usercopy(char *str)
 {
-	return strtobool(str, &enable_checks);
+	if (strtobool(str, &enable_checks))
+		pr_warn("Invalid option string for hardened_usercopy: '%s'\n",
+			str);
+	return 1;
 }
 
 __setup("hardened_usercopy=", parse_hardened_usercopy);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `mm/usercopy.c`**
- The function `parse_hardened_usercopy` was modified:
  - The return statement was changed from returning the result of `strtobool(str, &enable_checks)` to always returning `1`.
  - A warning message was added to print if `strtobool()` returns an error, indicating an invalid option string for `hardened_usercopy`.

### Relationships
- The modification in `mm/usercopy.c` ensures that the command line option `hardened_usercopy` is always acknowledged as handled (returning `1`), which prevents unknown kernel command line parameters from being passed to user space. This change addresses the issue of environment pollution during the initialization process when invalid options are provided. The warning mechanism provides feedback without affecting the command line handling logic.

but when "hardened_usercopy=foo" is used, there is no Unknown kernel

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `parse_hardened_usercopy` function not properly handling invalid command line options for `hardened_usercopy`. When an unrecognized option was provided, it did not return a value indicating that the option was handled, leading to pollution of the init environment with unknown parameters. This could result in unexpected behavior during the initialization of the system.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int __init parse_hardened_usercopy(char *str)
 {
-	return strtobool(str, &enable_checks);
+	if (strtobool(str, &enable_checks))
+		pr_warn("Invalid option string for hardened_usercopy: '%s'\n",
+			str);
+	return 1;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
return strtobool(str, &enable_checks);
```
Reason:
The `strtobool` function is called without checking its return value, which means that if an invalid command line option is provided, the function may return an error. In such cases, the function does not return a value indicating that the option was handled, leading to pollution of the init environment with unknown parameters.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (strtobool(str, &enable_checks))
    pr_warn("Invalid option string for hardened_usercopy: '%s'\n", str);
return 1;
```
Reason:
The patch adds a check for the return value of `strtobool`. If it indicates an error, a warning is printed, but the function still returns `1`, indicating that the command line option has been handled. This prevents unknown parameters from polluting the init environment, thus fixing the bug.
